Clause is an exemption from a fee; the ontology has no linear-inch dimension field and no oversize charge amount, so the 62-inch condition cannot be evaluated and no remedy applies.
Clause is a fee exemption about checked oversize charges; it grants no claim remedy and the 62 linear inch dimension is not in the ontology.

Clause is a baggage fee/logistics statement about oversize charges; the ontology has no scuba-equipment or linear-inch dimension fact and the clause sets no dispute remedy, so it cannot be decided from ontology facts.
Clause concerns an oversize charge exemption for ski/snowboard equipment by linear inches; the ontology has no dimension or equipment-type fact and the remedy is a fee waiver not a claim outcome.

Clause is a fee exemption about checking oversize surfboards/paddleboards; it does not state a claim remedy and dimensions (linear inches) and board type are not in the ontology, so it cannot be decided from ontology facts.
Clause is a fee exemption, not a dispute remedy; the 62 linear inch dimension is not in the ontology and the only available remedy is 'none', so the rule cannot meaningfully decide a claim.

Clause defines how actual value is determined and places a documentation burden on the passenger; it does not set a decision or an amount computable from the ontology facts (no purchase price documentation or depreciation fact exists).

Clause defines timely-notice sufficiency but grants no remedy, and 'good cause' is undefined and cannot be decided from ontology facts; the only encodable element is a partial timeliness gate, so confidence is low.
The condition (bag tendered within minimum check-in times in Section 15.C) cannot be tested with ontology facts; no check-in time field exists, and an unconditional rule is not permitted.
The deadline depends on the ticket expiration date and the refund application date, neither of which exists in the ontology; only a non-decidable procedural deadline is stated.

Clause sets a filing window and procedure (in-person claim at arrival airport) but states no remedy or amount; the only encodable element is the 2-hour window, which is recorded above with reduced confidence.
Clause is a procedural reporting deadline that states no remedy or outcome; it cannot yield an approve, partial or deny decision from the ontology facts alone.

Clause restricts how a bonus travel certificate may be applied (to fees or specific purchases). It is not a claim-entitlement rule and the ontology has no BTC instrument or Vacations/cargo/partner purchase facts to evaluate it against; an unconditional rule would violate encoding rules.

The clause voids a bonus travel certificate if it was altered or fraudulently obtained or obtained in violation of Atmos Rewards membership conditions. The ontology has no fact recording alteration, fraud, illegal acquisition, or membership-condition violation for a BTC, so the condition cannot be decided from ontology facts and no deterministic rule can be written.
